- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) or after a sharp spike, especially if followed by a drop.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not overshoot 1–2 days after sentiment peaks.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, favor mean-reversion toward recent 7–14 day average rather than trend-following.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust downward for the remainder of the horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines, reduce forecast slope; if sentiment is negative but price holds, increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating support.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price; use sentiment as a modifier, not a driver, especially in low-volatility regimes.
